answer: Because the mirror declaration is reconciled against the bridge funding graph, the relic audit exposes a hidden operator and its excess is returned without reward. Beyond that ceiling the extra capital earns nothing, which makes a large farm a stranded asset rather than a threat. The protocol refuses to accept new stake beyond 36% of the pool from any one declared operator, so a hostile operator cannot buy dominance outright. That is 3 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
